newsitem.title: USA: Apache's strong Q4 spurs solid 96 results.
newsitem.headline: Apache's strong Q4 spurs solid 96 results.

text.p: Apache Corp said Thursday a stronger-than-expected fourth quarter spurred its solid performance in 1996, resulting in a five-fold increase in eqrnings per share to $1.42.

During the latest quarter, the company posted its highest quarterly oil and gas production and prices of the year, resulting in record quarter net income of $51.2 million, or $0.57 per share, which was six times greater than in 1995.
"Between rising oil production and higher commodity prices, Apache earned more in the month of December than we reported for all of 1995, chief executive Raymond Plank said.
"We expect our momentum to continue in 1997, given built-in production increases and our inventory of drilling opportunities," Plank said.
Apache posted its ninth consecutive year of reserve growth in 1996, the company said.

Total proved reserves rose 20 percent to a record 506.2 million barrels of oil equivalent, up from 420.6 million at year-end 1995, and were comprised of 235.3 million barrels of oil and 1.6 trillion cubic feet of gas.

Including results of drilling, revisions and net acquisitions, the company said, it replaced 257 percent of the year's production at an all-sources cost of $6.09 per barrel of oil equivalent. Excluding the merger with The Phoenix Resource Cos and the subsequent long-term gas sales contract for the Khalda Concession in Egypt, Apache's finding cost was $5.42 per barrel.
The company said its estimated reserve life rose to 9.3 years from 7.8 years, while the proportion of oil in its reserve mix increased to 46 percent from 40 percent.
Apache said international reserves now represent 18 percent of the company's total reserves, compared to less than five percent at year-end 1995.

Exploration and development expenditures increased to $463 million in 1996 from $293.1 million in 1995. Spending 1997 are budgeted to increase about 35 percent over 1996 levels with the emphasis on drilling. The capital budget will be reviewed quarterly in light of product price volatility.

Including the $331.2 million paid for oil and gas properties in the Phoenix merger, acquisition expenditures in 1996 totaled $446.2 million, compared with $820.9 million in 1995, Apache's most active year for transactions.
